description: Guide the student to aggregate tick-level data into OHLCV bars, save the result as a CSV file, and apply proper timestamp handling and microstructure quality checks.
student_opening: My professor asked us to aggregate tick-level data into OHLCV bars, save the result. I'm new to both Python and finance — can you start from the basics?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Tutor guides the student to resample tick-level data into OHLCV bars and save the aggregated bars as a CSV file, handle timestamp quality issues, and validate bar quality with microstructure awareness.
required_capabilities: Resample tick-level data into OHLCV bars and save the result
Handle timestamp quality issues such as ordering and duplicates
Explain session/timezone boundaries and microstructure caveats
ground_truth.termination_criteria: (1) Showed actual resampling or aggregation output converting tick-level data into OHLCV bars using pandas resample, groupby, or equivalent code, and saved the result as a CSV file in the workspace. (2) Demonstrated concrete timestamp handling such as sorting, deduplication, or timezone normalization on the tick data, with before-and-after output showing the fix. (3) Responded to a student follow-up with one additional quality check or microstructure caveat on the aggregated bars, such as checking for empty bars, volume consistency, or session boundary alignment. Once all 3 steps have been computationally demonstrated, the session is complete.
